claims.text: Strain governs the catalytic activity of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Mixing governs the catalytic activity of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Surface composition governs the catalytic activity of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Strain, mixing, and surface composition synergistically govern the selectivity of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Strain, mixing, and surface composition synergistically govern the durability of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Multiobjective optimization and machine learning can optimize the strain, mixing, and surface composition of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Multiobjective optimization and machine learning can modify the composition and structure of high-entropy alloy catalysts.
Optimizing high-entropy alloy catalysts can produce a balance among catalytic activity, cost-effectiveness, and entropic stabilization.
The synergistic effects of strain, mixing, and surface composition improve catalytic activity.
The synergistic effects of strain, mixing, and surface composition improve catalytic selectivity.
The synergistic effects of strain, mixing, and surface composition improve catalyst durability.
Optimized high-entropy alloy catalysts will have greater catalytic activity than traditional catalysts with similar composition and structure.
Optimized high-entropy alloy catalysts will have greater selectivity than traditional catalysts with similar composition and structure.
Optimized high-entropy alloy catalysts will have greater durability than traditional catalysts with similar composition and structure.
The proposed relationships should hold across relevant catalytic temperatures, pressures, and electrolyte compositions.
The proposed relationships should hold for high-entropy alloy catalysts with varying compositions and structures.
